analysis:
The PR raises NemotronSuperServingPolicy.maximumEncodedBodyBytes from 8 MiB to 40 MiB (NemotronSuperServingPolicy.swift ~line 369). In NemotronSuperLocalImageBinding.swift it adds Failure.bodyTooLarge (head 17-18) and splits the encodedHeaderQuote guard (head 224-228). The template bound (1 MiB) and the bodyBytes > 0 check are preserved. The size check still runs before any reservation, JSON parse or decode (runEncoded, head 89), so oversize input is rejected up front and fails closed.

Security-relevant effect: the ingress charge is bodyBytes*32 + templateBytes*4 + 16 MiB. At the new cap this is about 1.28 GiB, up from about 272 MiB. It is reserved on the shared VisionMemoryGate/GlobalKVCacheBudget ledger (head 96), and a failed reserve throws Failure.capacity. This is an availability trade-off relevant to T-010/T-029. A consumer able to submit large inline-media bodies could hold a larger share of the shared budget during parsing, and could briefly crowd out text KV admission. Mitigations visible in this file are: one media request at a time (the `active == nil` guard, head 88); the reservation is released in settle (head 163-171) except on a retained fault; and capacity refusal fails closed. The gate's behaviour on starvation of concurrent text requests, and the true peak memory against the 32x multiplier for 32 MiB JSON/base64 bodies, are not in the supplied evidence. The stated 32 MiB transport limits (localInferenceMaxUploadBytes, CoordinatorClient.maxInboundMessageBytes) are asserted only in a comment and not verified here.

The new bodyTooLarge case may need mapping in callers (error propagation to the coordinator or local API). Those callers are outside this batch, so I cannot confirm that no switch falls through unsafely or leaks detail. No change touches the encryption, attestation, authorization or prefix-cache scope paths (T-041 cacheScope handling is unchanged). The next pass should check the memory-gate sizing and the caller handling of the new Failure case.
